newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel cabinet approves settlement incentives.
newsitem.headline: Israel cabinet approves settlement incentives.

text.p: The Israeli cabinet decided on Friday to grant special financial incentives to bolster Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank, a cabinet minister said.

At its weekly session two days after Arab guerrillas killed two Jewish settlers, the cabinet agreed that settlers would again enjoy tax breaks cancelled by the previous Labour-led government, Tourism Minister Moshe Katzav said.
"We have to find ways to implement this decision," Katzav told Israeli Army Radio.

The radio said a special ministerial committee would decide how to pay for the benefits at a time when the government had decided to cut state spending in the 1997 budget by 6.1 billion shekels ($1.9 billion).

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared at the funeral on Thursday of two Jewish settlers killed by Palestinian gunmen near PLO-ruled Ramallah in the West Bank that he would strengthen settlements despite Arab and international protests.
The government decision gives Jewish settlements equal footing with so-called development towns in Israel whose residents enjoy tax breaks, housing grants and preferential mortgage terms.
